blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for legal transcription

Your Mac needs to be a stable environment for long sessions of typing and editing. Start by ensuring your version of Microsoft Word is current. As of October 2026, the standalone version is 16.114.1. Keep your macOS updated to at least Sequoia, Tahoe, or Golden Gate to ensure you receive all security patches. This is vital when you handle sensitive attorney-client information.

Many transcriptionists struggle with Word crashing or freezing. If you notice the app becoming sluggish, go to your Applications folder and check for updates. If issues persist, you can reset your preferences or use Disk Utility to run First Aid on your drive. These steps often resolve the grayed-out menu items that prevent you from saving or editing your documents.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for faster typing

Efficiency comes from keeping your fingers on the home row. On your Mac, the Command key is your primary tool. Use ⌘ + S to save often. Use ⌘ + C and ⌘ + V for standard copy and paste. To move through a transcript quickly, use Option + Arrow Keys to jump by word. Use Command + Arrow Keys to jump to the start or end of a line.

items: Jump to start of line: ⌘ + Left Arrow
Jump to end of line: ⌘ + Right Arrow
Jump to previous word: ⌥ + Left Arrow
Jump to next word: ⌥ + Right Arrow
Select text by word: ⇧ + ⌥ + Arrow Keys

blocks.text: Mastering formatting in Word for Mac

Legal documents require strict adherence to formatting rules. If you need to create a table of contents, use the References tab to automate the process. For page numbering, use the Insert > Page Numbers menu. If you find yourself manually adjusting margins or headers for every document, create a custom template instead. This ensures every new file starts with the correct font, spacing, and layout.
If you are struggling to find a specific formatting option, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where it is. It will circle the correct button on your screen so you can find it instantly.

blocks.text: Handling sensitive data on your Mac

Privacy is the priority. Many transcriptionists prefer local, on-device tools to ensure audio and transcript data never leave their Mac. If you use cloud-based services, verify their subprocessor list to ensure they meet your firm's compliance standards. Always password-protect your final documents. You can do this by going to File > Passwords in Word.

items: Using manual spaces instead of tabs for alignment.
Hard-coding page breaks instead of using section breaks.
Failing to use Styles for headers, which breaks the document structure.
Overlooking inconsistent font sizes in copied citations.
Ignoring the document inspector for hidden metadata.

faq.question: Does Word for Mac support all the same macros as Windows?
faq.answer: No. There are differences in feature parity between the two platforms. Some advanced VBA macros or specific add-ins available on Windows may not function on the Mac version.

faq.question: How can I make my Mac run Word more reliably?
faq.answer: Keep your macOS updated and ensure you are using the latest version of Microsoft 365. If the app crashes, try force-quitting and restarting. If problems continue, check your system permissions or reset your Word preferences.

faq.question: Is it safe to use AI tools for legal transcription?
faq.answer: It depends on your firm's policy. Many professionals use on-device tools to maintain attorney-client privilege. Always review the privacy policy of any tool to ensure it does not use your data to train models.
